archetype: Mono-red Goblin swarm with a storm half bolted to it: token pressure and each-opponent reach on the floor, a copy/draw/storm burst turn as the ceiling

role_assignment.default_role: Beatdown-leaning swarm that paces toward one burst turn. Per-seat correction applies: against slower engine decks you are the beatdown and must pressure early (goldfish: early token maker drawn by mean turn 3.18, 60.0% of runs, 48.7% by turn 6); against a faster combo deck you are pushed into the racing-control seat and your reach has to be aimed rather than accumulated. Role is seat-relative and re-asked every turn cycle (strategy:whos-the-beatdown).
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Two independent triggers, and the deck does not need both. (a) Zada online with a payload spell — 66.1% of runs, 49.6% by turn 6, mean turn 5.27 — which is the verified one-mana mass-draw payload (stack 001). (b) A storm payoff with a ritual in hand — 26.5% of runs, 16.9% by turn 6, mean turn 4.91 — which needs no commander at all: of the passing stacks only 001 and 003 put Zada on the board, 002 resolves off Impact Tremors, 005 off Storm-Kiln Artist, and 004 states outright that she is in the command zone. Fire when the table's instant-speed interaction is spent or tapped; a telegraphed sweeper forces the half-go early, taking value or a wide board now rather than holding for a lethal that never gets cheaper (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math).

engines.engine: Copy hub: an instant or sorcery targeting only Zada is copied for each other creature you control. With the cantrips (Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Renegade Tactics, Witch's Mark, Fists of Flame) every body becomes a card; with Ancestors' Aid every body becomes a Treasure; with Wild Ride or Haze of Rage every body becomes damage.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 — four Goblin tokens plus a one-mana Crimson Wisps targeting only Zada draws five cards and hastes the team; oracle text

engines.engine: A second copy hub that routes through no legendary creature: it makes a hasty Soldier whenever you cast a spell targeting only a single creature you control, then copies that spell at the new token. It is the deck's answer to having its hub answered — redundancy in the effect class rather than a tutor for one card.
engines.evidence: oracle text (enchantment, {2}{R}); the redundancy pricing that makes an effect class rather than a named card the unit of consistency

engines.engine: The self-sustaining storm loop: buyback Haze of Rage recast at a rising storm count, magecraft minting a Treasure on every cast and every copy. Cast #1 as the fourth spell makes 3 copies and 4 Treasures; cast #2 makes 4 copies and 5 Treasures; every iteration costs 4 Treasures and yields k+3, so the loop is mana-positive and strictly improves.
engines.evidence: verified stack 005 (checker verdict pass) — 'the loop is mana-positive from here (sacrifice 4 Treasures per cast, gain k+3) and strictly improves each iteration'; combo_details records this pair as a bracket-3 two-card infinite

engines.engine: Storm tokens converted straight into each-opponent damage. Impact Tremors is the payoff that scales against three seats; General Kreat, the Boltbringer is the same trigger on a body, and Grapeshot rides the same storm count from the other side.
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 — Empty the Warrens as the fourth spell storm-triggers for 3 copies, 8 Goblin tokens enter, Impact Tremors deals 8 to each opponent, and a following Grapeshot sees storm count 4

engines.engine: The finisher on top of the copy hub: copies resolve one at a time and each draws, so each later copy locks in a bigger +1/+0-per-card-drawn with trample. An unassuming board becomes burst lethal in one cast.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 — sequential per-resolution buff sizing confirmed; earlier copies' buffs do not grow retroactively

engines.engine: A bounded burst, not a loop: Krenko cast for {1}{R}{R} under Goblin Warchief taps immediately for five tokens off a four-Goblin board, leaving ten Goblins with haste, and Prospector converts up to ten of them into one-shot red mana this phase. Treat it as a storm-count and mana spike aimed at a payoff already in hand.
engines.evidence: verified stack 004 — the combo_details 'infinite' presumes Krenko is the commander so 903.9a can loop him; Zada is the commander here, so a sacrificed Krenko stays in the graveyard and the line terminates after one cast, one activation, and at most ten red mana

engines.piece: Battle Hymn / Brightstone Ritual / Seething Song / Mana Geyser
engines.engine: The ritual base, and it scales off the swarm rather than off lands: Battle Hymn adds {R} per creature and Brightstone Ritual {R} per Goblin on the battlefield, so bodies are mana. This is what makes the storm turn possible at 4.59 mean available mana on turn 5.
engines.evidence: oracle text; goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn['5'] = 4.589 and land_drop_hit_rate_by_turn['5'] = 0.637; deck-audit engine component of 4 cards, 25.8% in an opener, 32.1% by turn three

engines.engine: Attrition-proof draw: the 1/1 tokens the deck manufactures die to the -1 toughness and pay two cards each for {1}. It is the reason a sweeper is a draw step rather than a loss.
engines.evidence: oracle text (equipped creature gets +1/-1; whenever equipped creature dies, draw two cards; equip {1})

engines.piece: Goblin Bombardment + Pashalik Mons + Boggart Shenanigans
engines.engine: Free-outlet reach: leftover tokens become damage at instant speed, dodging exile and bounce answers to the board, and Boggart Shenanigans turns each Goblin death into a point aimed at a player. This is how a swept or chump-blocked swarm still converts.
engines.evidence: oracle text all three; Goblin Bombardment's one in-deck synergy_graph partner is Mogg War Marshal (Sac + Death Trigger, Tokens + Sacrifice, Sac + ETB)

engines.engine: The whole protection budget: 2 copies against deck-audit's 5-7 target. The insurance question is priced against the recast tax rather than assumed — the storm half functions with Zada in the command zone, so hexproof is bought for the Zada draw turns specifically, not held every game.
engines.evidence: deck-audit protection axis: 2 copies, verdict under, target 5-7; oracle text (hexproof and haste, equip {1})

candidate_missing_lines.title: Past in Flames rebuilds the ritual chain for a second payoff
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: no combo_details record exists for Past in Flames (by_card lookup returns nothing), but the oracle text is direct — every instant and sorcery in the graveyard gains flashback at its mana cost — and stack 002's board already shows Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual in the graveyard mid-storm-turn. Recast rituals raise the storm count again for a second Grapeshot or Empty the Warrens. The open questions a scenario must settle are the exact storm count the second payoff sees and whether the mana actually nets positive

candidate_missing_lines.title: Roaming Throne naming Goblin doubles Zada's copy trigger
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: oracle text: Zada is a Legendary Creature — Goblin Ally and her copy ability is a triggered ability ('Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada'); Roaming Throne makes a triggered ability of another creature of the chosen type trigger an additional time. Whether the second trigger produces a second full set of copies, and what each copy then targets, is exactly what a scenario must resolve. Roaming Throne appears in no combo line contained in this deck

candidate_missing_lines.title: Frontline Heroism and Zada triggering off the same cantrip
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: both are cast-triggers on the same spell: Frontline Heroism creates a Soldier token and then copies the spell at that token, while Zada copies for each other creature that the spell could target. You control the order of your own triggers, so whether the Soldier that Frontline Heroism just made is counted by Zada's copy set depends on which trigger resolves first — a difference of one card per cast, and the kind of ordering question that decides a lethal turn

candidate_missing_lines.title: Ancestors' Aid on Zada as a ritual rather than a pump spell
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: oracle text: Ancestors' Aid targets a creature and creates a Treasure token, so each Zada copy that resolves should create its own Treasure — {1}{R} for one Treasure per other creature, which on a four-body board is mana-positive and, with Storm-Kiln Artist out, adds a magecraft Treasure per copy on top (stack 005 establishes that magecraft sees copies, not only casts). The count of Treasures produced and whether the mana arrives in time to matter that turn is what needs resolving

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Assume the wrath and size the commitment to it — over a four-player game one is near-certain, so deploy in waves and hold a rebuild package (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). This deck buys resilience rather than restraint: Skullclamp turns a swept board into cards, Goblin Bombardment and Pashalik Mons turn it into damage on the way out, and Mogg War Marshal and Rundvelt Hordemaster replace themselves. Against a control deck holding back IS the loss, because buying time is their plan. The telegraphed sweeper is also the canonical forced half-go — fire the cantrip engine now and bank the draws rather than hold for a lethal that never gets cheaper (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes attack this deck's velocity math directly: the plan is many cheap spells per turn, and a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine — recount your hand under the tax before you commit (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Role is forced: you do not own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown racing the lock's completion (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). Name the out early and sequence to protect it — Vandalblast (overload {4}{R}), Goblin Trashmaster, Chaos Warp — the piece that beats you, not the scariest piece (strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs). Deck-audit's breadth axis is honest about the exposure: 2 classes answered against a 5 target, with enchantment, graveyard and land uncovered.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Take the control seat here. Your bodies are replaceable and theirs are not: goldfish mean bodies 4.07 by turn 5 and 5.26 by turn 6 gives you a blocking wall while the engine sets up, Blasphemous Act costs {1} less per creature on the battlefield and is near-free against a wide board, and Gempalm Incinerator cycles for damage equal to your Goblin count. Rank by clock and by what actually beats you rather than by what looks scary (strategy:threat-assessment), and let 40 life absorb the early turns while you keep the pivot window intact.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Held answers rot against combo — the last profitable moment is now (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Rank combo proximity above every board threat and apply pressure so their tapped-out setup turn is punished; Grenzo, Havoc Raiser's goad mode points other players' creatures away from you and their cast-from-exile mode converts combat damage into resources. Your interaction is real but narrow — deck-audit counts 13 interactive copies across only two permanent classes, and zero sweepers — so plan to disrupt once, cheaply, at the decisive moment rather than to out-race a dedicated combo deck. Your own storm assembly is a 26.5% line at mean turn 4.91, which is a live ceiling and not a clock you can promise the table.

distribution_notes: The curve is radically low: 15 one-drops, 19 twos, 13 threes, 10 fours, 6 fives and a single nine (Blasphemous Act, which costs {1} less per creature on the battlefield), modal mana value 2. Mana is 36 land copies across 15 entries plus 43 total red sources against a Karsten target of 36, with 5 lands that always enter tapped — deck-audit reads mana-base, mana-sources, taplands and colour-sources all at target under the aggro template, and creatures at 27 inside the 26-32 band. What is under target is the interaction profile: card-advantage 8 against 10 (with Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Fountainport, Gempalm Incinerator, Renegade Tactics and War Room drawing cards the taxonomy does not classify as draw), protection 2 against 5-7, threat-density 2 against 3, sweepers 0, and interaction-breadth 2 classes against 5. Ramp reads 15 against 10-12, which is the ritual base being counted as ramp rather than an excess. On speed: keep-first-seven 79.1%, mean mulligans 0.26, commander mean cast turn 4.35 (median 4, 90% by turn 6), mean available mana 4.59 on turn 5 with land-drop hit rate down to 63.7% — so the big turns are ritual-funded, not land-funded. The three declared engines sit at 66.1% (Zada plus a payload, 6 cards, thinnest component, 36.4% in an opener), 60.0% (early token maker, 5 cards, 31.2%) and 26.5% (storm payoff plus ritual, two 4-card components at 25.8% each). That last figure is the ceiling line and it is an AND of two independent draws, which is why it sits at a quarter of runs while each half sits near a third by turn three. Read against the redundancy table — 5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%, 10 is 54% (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors) — every component here is in the 4-6 band, i.e. built for one of the pieces to show up, not for a specific one.
overall_assessment: This is a linear deck in Duke's sense — every card feeds one plan, and the plan is reaching the threshold where the synergies take over (strategy:critical-mass). Its interaction slots are the price of the engine, which is exactly what deck-audit measures when it puts breadth at two classes and sweepers at zero: the defense is speed, redundancy and resilience, not answers. The pilot's craft is separating ceiling from median and pacing for the median (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math). The median game is the goblin swarm plus the Zada draw engine — bodies by turn 3, a payload spell by turn 5, cards and haste for one red mana (verified stack 001). The ceiling is the storm turn: a payoff and a ritual together in 26.5% of runs at mean turn 4.91, and once Storm-Kiln Artist is on the board with Haze of Rage in hand it is not a burst but a loop that strictly improves each iteration (verified stack 005). Crucially the two halves are independent. Only one of the three declared engines is commander-gated, and three of the five passing stacks resolve without Zada on the battlefield — 002 off Impact Tremors, 005 off Storm-Kiln Artist, 004 with her explicitly in the command zone. That independence is the deck's real resilience: killing the hub costs you the draw engine and not the kill, and Frontline Heroism is a second hub in the same effect class. Against three seats the Philosophy of Fire's raw cards-to-damage math collapses at ~120 combined life, so the payoffs that count are the ones that hit every seat at once — Impact Tremors and General Kreat pinging each opponent per body, Grapeshot off the storm count, a wide hasted alpha strike (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire, strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry). Politically the board reads as 1/1s until the turn it wins, which is the deflection posture to cultivate: sequence Krenko, Storm-Kiln Artist and Conspicuous Snoop after the table's removal is spent, and time the tells for the turn they win rather than the turn they impress (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection). Mulligan to the enabler class, not the named card — a hand of payoffs with no ritual and no cantrip is a ship despite its card quality (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands) — and commit fully only in the window where the table's interaction is counted and accounted for (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).
gaps: No goad or forced-combat section — Grenzo, Havoc Raiser compels an opponent's creature to attack elsewhere, which is compulsion rather than persuasion; strategy:multiplayer.politics covers deals and perceived threat but not effects that remove the choice

No aristocrats / sacrifice-conversion section — the theory of free outlets (Goblin Bombardment, Skirk Prospector, Skullclamp) turning a board that is about to die into mana, cards or damage, and how that changes overextension math, has no home in the doc

No section on hub redundancy for a copy or trigger engine specifically — strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices effect classes and strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices protecting the commander, but neither covers a non-legendary duplicate of the hub (Frontline Heroism standing in for Zada) as a distinct consistency purchase
